tagline: A real person in a real studio
sector: An independent maker and lifestyle creator in Portland selling small-batch stoneware, with a seasonal coffee-bar collaboration each autumn.
founded_place_size: Quill and Kiln, founded 2020, Portland, Oregon, a one-maker studio working from a shared space, with roughly nine thousand followers.
about: Marlo Quill makes small-batch stoneware in a shared Portland studio and sells it four times a year, plus a coffee-bar collaboration each autumn. About a third of what she sells comes straight off her own posts. The brand is the person: a real maker in a real room, warm and quiet, and never a polished label, because that is what her audience follows her for.
audience: Followers aged 22 to 34, the same age as Marlo, who buy 38 to 90 dollar stoneware and follow the maker rather than a brand.
price_positioning: A mid-tier creator retainer of 600 to 1,500 dollars a month, stoneware at 38 to 90 dollars. Above careless untreated phone photos, below gallery-ceramics gloss; a heavy uniform filter would read as selling out and cost her directly.
typography: A warm humanist serif with a hand feel for names and headings, paired with a simple unfussy sans for captions and prices. A maker's hand rather than an agency deck.
voice: First person, casual and direct. Example line: One look, mine, not a filter.
brand_assets_status: No formal brand files. Her three motifs, a mug, a sprig and a small kiln, exist only as ink on a photographed sketchbook page she keeps re-cropping. The true glaze colours are pinned by a single reference frame of fired test tiles rather than any spec, and there is no logo file.
values: One recognisable hand across the whole feed, with real rooms, true glaze colours and her own drawn marks.
